recipe.title: Pork Tenderloin with Creamy Dijon Leek Sauce
recipe.description: Pan‑seared pork tenderloin medallions served with a silky leeks and Dijon mustard cream sauce, accompanied by sautéed green beans.
instructions: Trim the pork tenderloin, cut into 4 equal medallions about 2 cm thick; pat dry with paper towels.
Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 c. à soupe olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the pork medallions and sear 3 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 60 °C; remove and keep warm.
In the same skillet, add 1 c. à soupe butter, thinly sliced shallots and the white‑and‑light‑green parts of the leeks (cleaned and sliced). Sauté 4 minutes, stirring, until softened and fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with 2 c. à soupe water (or dry white wine if available), scraping up browned bits.
Stir in the cream and Dijon mustard, bring to a gentle simmer and reduce for 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon.
Season the sauce with additional salt and pepper to taste.
While the sauce simmers, blanch the green beans in boiling salted water 3 minutes, then shock in ice water; drain and pat dry.
Sauté the green beans in a separate pan with a splash of olive oil over medium heat 4 minutes, until just tender and lightly browned; season with salt.
Plate the pork medallions, spoon the creamy Dijon leek sauce over them, and serve with the sautéed green beans on the side.
tips: Do not over‑cook the pork; a slight pink centre keeps it juicy.
Use the green parts of the leeks for a milder flavor; reserve the dark green leaves for stock if desired.

recipe.description: Thinly sliced pork tenderloin wrapped in a crisp, golden Gruyère cheese crust, baked and served with a light shallot‑green bean vinaigrette.

Meanwhile, trim the green beans, blanch 3 minutes in salted water, drain and shock in ice water.
Finely mince the shallots; whisk together 2 c. à soupe olive oil, the minced shallots, chopped parsley, a pinch of salt, and pepper to make a quick vinaigrette.
Toss the blanched green beans with the vinaigrette just before serving.
Slice the baked pork logs into medallions and arrange on plates beside the dressed green beans.
tips: Grating the cheese finely helps it melt and stick, creating a uniform crust.
If the cheese crust browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil for the last 5 minutes.
